prize_parts.citation: for the theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of the quantum spin Hall effect and time-reversal-invariant topological insulators

statement.case_for: After reading all eight ballots I am moving my preferred prize from my own first-place choice, B009 (IceCube), to B050. B050 is the only shortlisted candidate that six of eight members ranked, four of them in their top three, and all six proposed the identical trio. That convergence is not merit in itself, but the arguments behind it hold up. Kane and Mele supplied a clean, original prediction (the Z2 classification and the quantum spin Hall state), and Molenkamp's HgTe experiment gave a measurable quantised edge conductance that tested it. The field has been confirmed independently in 2D and 3D materials by transport and ARPES for well over a decade, so the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely, arguably overdue. As an experimentalist I value that the theory made a sharp, falsifiable prediction that an instrument-driven experiment then verified.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed the HgTe quantum well route that Molenkamp realised, and Fu, Kane, Moore, Balents and others carried the idea to three dimensions, so a three-name prize leaves out contributors whom a careful historian would put close to the centre. A second concern is overlap with the 2016 prize for topological phases and phase transitions: the committee would need to argue that the symmetry-protected spin Hall and Z2 results are a distinct achievement, not an extension. Finally, B050 is the safe consensus choice and I should not mistake safety for being the best science on the list.

responses.point: Eriksson ranked B050 first as a conceptually clean discovery whose symmetry-based classification now underpins how topological band structure is computed and screened, and accepts the three-name credit while noting the omission of the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and 3D contributors.
responses.response: I agree on the conceptual value and on the stability of the framework, and I share the worry about the omitted names. I would qualify one thing: the later classification and DFT screening work is a consequence of the discovery and should not be credited in the citation, so I would keep the citation to the quantum spin Hall prediction and the HgTe observation. That keeps the 2016 overlap question narrow and defensible.

responses.point: Danielsson ranked B003 (inflation) first but placed B050 second, calling it conceptually clear and mature, and made the point that Kane and Mele are decisive theorists with Molenkamp delivering the experiment.
responses.response: I take his support for B050 as a real signal given that his first choice was elsewhere. I disagree with ranking B003 above it for this year: by his own account inflation is not uniquely established, primordial B-modes are unseen, and credit is entangled with Starobinsky outside the credited names. The perturbation spectrum is well measured, but the mechanism is still open, so I see B050 as the sounder choice now, even though inflation is the larger idea.

responses.point: Lindroth ranked the optical lattice clock B051 first as a mature, demanding instrument with reach into geodesy, constants tests and the redefinition of the second, and placed B050 fourth.
responses.response: I ranked B051 fifth and still regard it as a strong candidate, so I name it as my first alternative. My hesitation is the overlap with the 2005 frequency comb prize and the 2012 ion control prize, which she raises herself, and the pending redefinition of the second. She is right that the technology is mature and no longer speculative. Where I differ is that B050 has a cleaner prediction-then-experiment structure and a clearer claim to be a distinct discovery.

responses.point: Mehlig ranked B027 (ultracold atoms in optical lattices) first and B002 third, noting that B002 combines a clean theory with a decisive experiment but is young and the superconducting mechanism is unsettled.
responses.response: On B002 I agree with his maturity concern, which is why I keep it only as a second alternative and not as the preferred prize. On B027 I disagree that the three-person cut is workable: five credited names and heavy overlap with B015 in Cirac and Zoller make a defensible allocation hard, and I do not think the first-place support there outweighs that.

uncertainties: Whether the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (and the 3D contributors) is acceptable under a three-laureate limit, or whether it should push the committee to a different candidate.
Whether the 2016 topological phases prize makes B050 look incremental to the Academy.
Whether B051 should be preferred if the committee gives weight to the redefinition of the second reaching the formal stage.

I withdrew my own first choice B009 partly because its single-name credit under-represents a collaboration-scale discovery; I am relying on my own recollection of IceCube history and have not verified priority details.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B050, B051 or B002. My documented connections (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+, XL-Calibur, KTH astroparticle group) are in astroparticle instrumentation and would have been relevant only to B009 on field proximity, which I am no longer proposing.
